qs.q: The `href` attribute in the link tag specifies the:

c.x: Window in which the link opens

qs.e: The `href` attribute of the `` element holds the value of the page (URL) you are linking to, i.e. the destination of the link. The clickable text is the content between `` and ``.

qs.q: What is the correct HTML for creating a hyperlink?
qs.e: A link is made with the `<a>` element carrying an `href` attribute whose value is the target URL. The `name` attribute only creates an anchor point inside a page, `<a>` with no attribute links nowhere, and `url` is not a valid attribute.

qs.q: How can you create an e-mail link?
qs.e: An e-mail link is an ordinary anchor whose `href` value starts with `mailto:` followed by the address, e.g. `E-mail us`. Without `mailto:` the browser treats the value as a page address, and `` is not an HTML tag.

qs.q: Which attribute is used to display text if the picture could not be loaded in the browser?
qs.e: The `alt` attribute of the `` tag provides alternative text that is shown when the image is not supported or cannot be loaded. `src` gives the image file location, and `track` and `img` are not image attributes.

qs.q: Which attribute is used to specify the file of the image to display on the web page?
qs.e: In `` the `src` attribute gives the path of the image file. `alt` is only the fallback text, and `img` is the tag itself, not an attribute.

qs.q: Which HTML tag is used to display a picture in an HTML page?
qs.e: Images are inserted with the empty tag ``, written as ``. `src` is an attribute of ``, not a tag, and `` and `` are not the standard tag for inserting an image in the lecture syntax.

qs.q: Which of these tags are all table tags?
qs.e: A table is built with `<table>` containing rows `<tr>`, and each row contains cells `<td>` (or heading cells `<th>`). The other groups each include a tag that is not a table tag: `<head>`, `<tt>` (monospaced text) or `<body>`.

qs.q: The tag which allows you to provide a title (description) for a table is ______.
qs.e: `<caption>` adds a caption to a table. `<th>` is a heading cell, `<td>` is a data cell and `<tr>` is a table row.

qs.q: Which attribute is used with the `<td>` tag to merge two cells horizontally?
qs.e: `colspan="2"` makes a cell span two columns, which merges two cells horizontally (as in the Classic Movie Day table, where one movie occupies two time slots). `rowspan` merges cells vertically, and `merge` is not an attribute.

c.x: Used to separate cell walls from their contents
Used to set space between cells
Used to provide width to a cell

qs.e: The `cellpadding` attribute specifies the space between the content of a cell and the inside of the cell wall. The space between the cells themselves is `cellspacing`.

qs.q: The main container for `<tr>`, `<td>` and `<th>` is:
qs.e: A table is written inside the `<table>` element, row by row with `<tr>`, and each row contains `<td>` cells or `<th>` heading cells. `<group>` and `<data>` are not table tags, and `<form>` is used to collect user input.

qs.q: Can a data cell (`<td>`) contain images?
qs.e: A table cell can hold any content, including text, images and other markup, as in the quiz table whose cells contain building photographs with captions.

qs.q: Which tag does a description (definition) list start with?
qs.e: A definition list is contained inside the `<dl>` element, which holds alternating `<dt>` (term) and `<dd>` (definition) elements.

qs.q: How can you make a bulleted list with numbers?
qs.e: An ordered list `<ol>` prefixes each `<li>` item with numbers, letters or Roman numerals. `<ul>` gives bullet points, `<dl>` is a definition list and `<list>` does not exist.

qs.q: How can you make a bulleted list?
qs.e: The `<ul>` (unordered list) element creates a list of bullet points, with each point written in an `<li>` tag. `<ol>` creates a numbered list, and `<list>` and `<nl>` are not HTML tags.

qs.q: Which tag is used to create a numbered list?
qs.e: `<ol>` (ordered list) creates the numbered list; `<li>` only defines each item inside any list. `<ul>` produces bullets and `<dl>` produces terms with definitions.

qs.q: The tag used to create a new list item is ______.
qs.e: Each bullet or number in a `<ul>` or `<ol>` list is written with an `<li>` tag. `<dl>` and `<dd>` belong to definition lists, and `<ul>` is the list container.

qs.q: Which is the correct way to start an ordered list at the number 3?
qs.e: The `start` attribute of `<ol>` specifies the number a numbered list should start at, while `type` selects the numbering style ("1", "A", "a", "I", "i"). `initial`, `begin` and `num` are not valid attributes.

qs.q: The `<dt>` tag is designed to fit a single line of the web page, but the `<dd>` tag will accept a ______.
qs.e: In a definition list `<dt>` holds the short term, while `<dd>` holds its definition or description, which can be a full paragraph of text.
